mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of GDP growth than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals an improving labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of falling unemployment than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in the last two months signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increased industrial production than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 10% in the last two months signals a weakening in the housing market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of decreased housing starts than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and CPI inflation rises by more than 0.5% in the last month, the combination signals a tightening monetary environment with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of high rates and rising inflation than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in the last month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3%, the combined signal indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong labor market signals than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real retail and food services sales signals a strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increased retail sales than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
